**Finding**
- US 1400 (IC receivable from DE) = USD 10,450; DE 2300 (IC payable to US) = EUR 7,800 (USD 8,580 at 1.10). Gap of USD 1,870.
- Traced the US balance to four entries: two supported IC invoices (ICI-DE-01 EUR 7,800 @1.08 = 8,424; ICI-DE-02 EUR 500 @1.10 = 550), a correctly computed 3/31 remeasurement (+156, supported by the Treasury rate sheet), and a manual "IC adj DE per call" of USD 1,320 (JE-00306) with **no support, no invoice, and no EUR amount**.

**Booked on DE's side (supported)**
- **JE-00309** — DE, 2026-03-18: Dr 6200 Software Subscriptions / Cr 2300 Intercompany Payable **EUR 500**, support DOC-0190 (ICI-DE-02). Confirmed DE hadn't booked it elsewhere and that only two IC invoices to DE exist. DE 2300 now = EUR 8,300 = USD 9,130, which agrees to the cent with the supported portion of the US receivable.

**Escalated (EXC-001)**
- The entire residual USD 1,320 is JE-00306. Per policy, I did not post anything on DE's side to force agreement. The controller needs to either supply support (DE would then book EUR 1,200) or reverse JE-00306 in the US ledger — I can post that reversal on instruction.

**Checklist**
- DE Intercompany reconciliation → complete; US → blocked pending the JE-00306 decision.
